skill.name: enact-json-formatter
skill.description: Formats, validates, and prettifies JSON strings with configurable indentation.
skill.summary: Validate and format JSON strings with configurable indentation.
skill.author: EnactProtocol

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives from Markdown code fences and an output schema description. I found no prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or malicious behavior in the reviewed files.

static_findings.snippet: description: "Whether the input was valid JSON"

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 52 starts a Markdown bash example block in documentation. It is not executable skill code and does not run untrusted shell input.

content.value_statement: Compact JSON is hard to review, and invalid data slows debugging. This skill validates JSON and returns a clean, indented version with errors.
actual_capabilities: Parses JSON strings and reports whether they are valid.
Returns formatted JSON text using configurable spaces.
Uses a default two-space indentation when no indent is supplied.
Reports parse errors in structured output.
Runs locally with Node.js in a container command.
limitations: It does not repair malformed JSON.
It does not fetch remote files or URLs.
It accepts JSON as a string argument, so very large payloads may be unwieldy.
It formats data only; it does not validate business schemas.

use_cases.title: Review API responses
use_cases.description: Format minified response data before comparing fields or sharing examples.

use_cases.title: Check pasted data samples
use_cases.description: Validate JSON snippets before using them in reports or data tools.

use_cases.title: Prepare test fixtures
use_cases.description: Create readable JSON payloads for bug reports and regression tests.

prompt_templates.title: Format a JSON string
prompt_templates.prompt: Format this JSON with the default indentation. Return the formatted result and validation status.

prompt_templates.title: Use custom indentation
prompt_templates.prompt: Format this JSON with four-space indentation. If it is invalid, explain the parse error from the tool output.

prompt_templates.title: Validate an API response
prompt_templates.prompt: Validate this minified JSON from an API response, format it, and highlight whether parsing failed before I compare fields.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a testing payload
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the JSON formatter on this generated payload, preserve all values, and summarize any parse error before downstream testing.

output_examples.input: A minified configuration object pasted as one line.
output_examples.output: The tool returns a readable multi-line version and marks the input as valid.

output_examples.input: A pasted data sample with a missing closing marker.
output_examples.output: The tool marks the input as invalid and returns the parser error message.

output_examples.input: A valid payload requested with four-space indentation.
output_examples.output: The tool returns the same data values with wider indentation for team style review.

best_practices: Choose two-space indentation for shared configuration unless your team uses another standard.
Run invalid inputs through the tool before debugging downstream consumers.
Review parse errors before assuming an application bug.
anti_patterns: Do not use it to validate domain rules or required fields.
Do not paste secrets into sample JSON unless your environment permits it.
Do not assume formatting changes the data values.

faq.question: Does this skill validate JSON?
faq.answer: Yes. It parses the input and returns a valid flag with an error when parsing fails.

faq.question: Can I choose the indentation size?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide an indent value, or use the default two spaces.

faq.question: Does it change JSON values?
faq.answer: No. It parses and formats the same data values when the input is valid.

faq.question: Can it repair broken JSON?
faq.answer: No. It reports parse errors but does not rewrite invalid input into valid JSON.

faq.question: Does it access files or the network?
faq.answer: No evidence found. The implementation reads command arguments and prints structured output.

faq.question: Which assistants can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
